Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents a customer who places food orders, linked to their Google account for authentication.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

googleAccountId.description: Unique identifier provided by the Google authentication system for the customer.

name.description: Full name of the customer as provided in the order form.

email.description: Email address of the customer, used for communication.

phoneNumber.description: Contact phone number or WhatsApp number of the customer.

deliveryAddress.description: The default delivery address for the customer.

MenuItem.title: MenuItem
MenuItem.description: Represents a single food or drink item available on the Ramadhan Takjil menu.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MenuItem entity, often corresponding to the SKU.

name.description: The name of the menu item (e.g., 'Nasi Bakar Ayam').

price.description: The price of the menu item in Indonesian Rupiah (e.g., 12000).

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) for the menu item, used for identification (e.g., RpSKU-1).

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents a single customer order for Takjil items, including delivery and payment details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer who placed this order. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Order)

orderDateTime.description: The date and time when the order was placed.

totalAmount.description: The total monetary amount of the order, including all items and the delivery fee.

deliveryFee.description: The fixed delivery fee applied to this order (Rp. 2.500).

paymentMethod.description: The chosen payment method for the order.

status.description: The current processing status of the order.

deliveryAddress.description: The full delivery address specified for this particular order (copied from customer at order time).

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents a specific menu item and its quantity within a larger order.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrderItem entity.

orderId.description: Reference to the Order this item belongs to. (Relationship: Order 1:N OrderItem)

menuItemId.description: Reference to the MenuItem that was ordered. (Relationship: MenuItem 1:N OrderItem)

quantity.description: The quantity of the specific menu item included in the order.

priceAtOrder.description: The price of the menu item at the time the order was placed, to ensure historical accuracy.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for the Ramadhan Takjil Order application prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles. The primary strategy employed is **Authorization Independence via Denormalization** (Mandate A) and **Structural Segregation** (Mandate B), combined with **Access Modeling** using hierarchical paths for user-owned data (Mandate C).

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **Customer Profile (`/customers/{customerId}`):** The `customerId` wildcard directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`. The `Customer` document's `id` and `googleAccountId` fields will also store this UID. This means that to check if a user can access their profile, rules only need to compare `request.auth.uid` with the `customerId` in the path, and optionally `resource.data.googleAccountId`. No `get()` operations on parent documents are required.
2.  **Orders (`/customers/{customerId}/orders/{orderId}`):** Each `Order` document includes a `customerId` field. This denormalizes the ownership directly into the order document. Security rules for `Order` documents can therefore verify `request.auth.uid == customerId` (from the path) and `request.auth.uid == resource.data.customerId` without needing to perform a `get()` on the parent `/customers/{customerId}` document. This ensures atomic creation and updates and simplifies rules significantly.
3.  **Order Items (`/customers/{customerId}/orders/{orderId}/orderItems/{orderItemId}`):** Similarly, each `OrderItem` document will denormalize both `customerId` and `orderId` fields. Rules for `OrderItem` documents can check `request.auth.uid == customerId` (from the path), `resource.data.customerId`, and `resource.data.orderId` directly against the path segments, completely eliminating cross-document `get()` calls for authorization.

**QAPs (Queries as Authorization Primitives) and Structural Segregation:**
1.  **Menu Items (`/menuItems/{menuItemId}`):** This collection is designed for **homogeneous security posture**. All menu items are publicly readable, allowing any user (authenticated or unauthenticated) to browse the menu. This makes `list` operations on `/menuItems` inherently secure and efficient, as rules can simply grant `read` access to all. There's no mixing of public and private data in this collection.
2.  **Customer-Specific Data (`/customers/{customerId}/...`):** By nesting `orders` and `orderItems` under `/customers/{customerId}`, access is implicitly scoped to the authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`). A user can only `list` or `get` documents within their own `/customers/{request.auth.uid}/orders` or `/customers/{request.auth.uid}/orders/{orderId}/orderItems` subcollections. This prevents users from listing other customers' orders, effectively making `list` operations secure without complex filtering logic in rules. The path itself acts as a strong authorization primitive, aligning with the principle that 'rules are not filters'.

**Overall, the structure:**
*   Uses `request.auth.uid` as the primary identifier for customers and their data, making authorization direct.
*   Employs clear, hierarchical paths for user-owned data (`/customers/{userId}/orders/{orderId}/orderItems/{orderItemId}`).
*   Denormalizes critical authorization fields (`customerId`, `orderId`) into child documents to avoid expensive and insecure `get()` calls in security rules.
*   Separates public (menu items) from private (customer orders) data to simplify rules and support efficient `list` queries.
*   Adopts explicit state modeling for `Order.status` and predictable schemas to ensure data clarity and consistency.
